Uses of Package
io.mavlink4j.codec

Packages that use io.mavlink4j.codec
Package
Description
io.mavlink4j.codec
L2 — bytes to Frame and back, plus MAVLink 2 signing.
io.mavlink4j.service
L4 — one class per MAVLink microservice (command, parameter, heartbeat, manual control, message interval, capability).
io.mavlink4j.session
L3 — the MavlinkSession composition root: reader threads, peer directory, dispatcher, correlator, TX scheduler.
io.mavlink4j.testkit
Test doubles for code that talks MAVLink through mavlink4j, with no SITL, socket or hardware needed: a scripted FakeVehicle, in-memory links (RecordingLink, LoopbackLinkPair) and deterministic time (ManualInstantSource, DirectTxScheduler).
  • Classes in io.mavlink4j.codec used by io.mavlink4j.codec
    Class
    Description
    Frame
    One fully decoded MAVLink frame: header plus payload, stamped with where it came from.
    FrameHeader
    The wire-level facts of one MAVLink frame, decoded but not interpreted.
    SignatureRejection
    A frame FrameReader decoded but did not dispatch, because SignatureVerifier itself refused it or because SigningPolicy.accept(int, SignatureStatus) did, given a verifier result it chose not to accept.
    SignatureRejection.Reason
    Why the frame was refused.
    SignatureStatus
    The cryptographic-validity dimension of a decoded MAVLink 2 frame, orthogonal to FrameHeader.signed() (the raw wire bit).
    Signing
    The one collaborator bundle FrameReader/FrameWriter/ io.mavlink4j.session.MavlinkSession thread signing through: a key resolver, a policy and a clock registry.
    SigningClock
    The MAVLink 2 signing timestamp for one remote system (VERIFIED, mavlink.io message-signing spec): a 48-bit counter in 10 microsecond ticks since SigningClock.SIGNING_EPOCH, not Unix epoch -- a naive millisecond- or microsecond-since-1970 implementation produces a value that looks plausible and fails every verification silently (QA item 3).
    SigningClocks
    One SigningClock per remote system id -- a signing timestamp is a per-vehicle fact (two vehicles must never share a monotonic counter), never a process-wide one.
    SigningKeyResolver
    The sysid→key lookup the library cannot own: which 32-byte secret belongs to which vehicle is the host application's knowledge (a key store, a device registry), so the host supplies the implementation and the library only consumes the interface.
    SigningPolicy
    Decides whether a decoded frame is dispatched, given its origin sysid and SignatureStatus.
